What does Ambroxan smell like?

Ambergris, woody and dry with a labdanum warmth, a soft marine-mineral salinity and a light sweetness. Radiant and long-lasting; the backbone of modern amber and skin-scent perfumery, from traces to bold overdoses.

Use Ambroxan in a formula

How do you use Ambroxan in a perfume?

Read from this material's catalog record and PerfuMate's published formulas.

  • It is a base note: it holds the drydown and anchors the faster materials above it. On a blotter it lasts about 17 days.
  • Its impact is 7 of 10: medium. Trial it at a modest share first and raise it on the strip rather than by guess.
  • In 8 published formulas, most of them accords, it makes up 1.4% to 31.5% of the concentrate (median 9.7%). An accord is one part of a perfume, so expect a smaller share in a finished formula.
  • Weigh it neat, or from a 10% dilution when you need small amounts; both are common on the bench. The free dilution calculator does the arithmetic.
  • In the published formulas it sits most often beside Iso E Super, Habanolide, Vanillin and Ambrettolide.
